plan.concept: Discrete entropy H = -sum p_i log2 p_i as a measure of choice/uncertainty, its properties (H=0 iff certain, H=log2 n when uniform), and correct handling of zero probabilities.
plan.anchor: Section 6, Theorem 2: H = -K sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i log p_i; with base-2 logs the unit is the bit.
plan.computation: From the probability vector p (normalized), compute each term -p_i log2 p_i (with the limit 0 when p_i=0), the total H, the maximum log2 n, the deficit log2 n - H, and the uniform reference value.
plan.visual: Left: bar chart of probabilities p_i with the uniform level 1/n marked. Right: stacked/individual contribution bars -p_i log2 p_i plus a total-entropy bar, with the log2 n ceiling line.
plan.controls: n (number of outcomes), a probability vector of length n (resized with n), a 'uniform' toggle that sets all p_i equal, and a select for a two-outcome p vs 1-p view.
plan.checks: Certainty gives 0 bits; four equally likely outcomes give 2 bits; H >= 0 always; H <= log2 n; zero probabilities contribute 0; uniform maximizes H.
